newsitem.title: USA: Rykoff-Sexton sees Q1 at breakeven.
newsitem.headline: Rykoff-Sexton sees Q1 at breakeven.

text.p: Rykoff-Sexton Inc said Thursday it expects to report breakeven to moderately profitable results for the first quarter ending September 28, 1996.
For the newly adopted fiscal year ending June 28, 1997, the company expects earnings to approximate $0.50 to $0.60 per share.

For the prior fiscal year ended April 27, 1996, it earned $0.07 per share, excluding a non-cash charge of $1.19 per share from an accounting rule relating to the carrying value of certain long-lived assets.
Rykoff-Sexton said earnings per share expectations for fiscal year 1997 reflect non-cash goodwill amortization of about $0.35 to $0.40 per share.
Fiscal 1996 reflected the non-cash amortization of goodwill of $0.04 per share.
It said current analysts' estimates for the 1997 fiscal year range from $0.45 to $1.25 per share.

"Our company is moving swiftly to effect cost savings by closing and consolidating a number of distribution centers throughout the country and taking other measures to maximize synergies," said president Frank Bevevino in a statement. He added that quarterly results will be progressively higher as the year unfolds.
The merger between Rykoff-Sexton and US Foodservice Inc in May created the nation's third largest broadline foodservice distribution company, with sales of about $3.5 billion.
